opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Black (employee ID E008) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E008.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Employee E008 (Karen Black) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Source Code. Full-time employees can have up to write; admin requires the employee's role to own the system (Source Code is owned by Engineer). Since requested admin exceeds the maximum, recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E008 (Karen Black) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds max of read, so recommend read. This differs from the prior note's full-time classification.
reason: Karen Black (E008) requested admin access to Source Code, but the notes conflict on her employment classification: HR's note says full-time (max write, admin only if role owns the system; Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code), while Security's note says contractor with basic training (max read). Admin is not permitted under either scenario. To avoid granting a level that would violate policy under the contractor classification while remaining valid under the full-time classification, I grant the conservative maximum that is safe in both cases: read.
